evals.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow for a Node.js project. It should run on pull requests and pushes to main, install with npm ci, and run npm test. Save the workflow as ci.yml.
evals.expected_output: A maintainable CI workflow that uses explicit read permissions, concurrency cancellation, npm caching, a timeout, and clear job/step names.
expectations: The workflow runs `npm ci` as the install step and `npm test` as the test step, as the prompt asked; a substituted command (`npm install`, `npm run test:ci`) fails this.
The workflow sets explicit least-privilege permissions rather than relying on GitHub defaults.
The workflow defines concurrency with cancel-in-progress for superseded branch or PR runs.
The Node setup uses npm caching or an equivalent package-manager cache.
The test job has a timeout and clear names for the workflow, job, and key steps.

The produced or corrected workflow YAML passes actionlint, zizmor (regular persona), poutine, and `pinact run -check -verify-comment -min-age 7 -verify-min-age` with zero findings when the grader runs them on the output, except poutine `default_permissions_on_risky_events` on a job whose `permissions: {}` is explicit (known false positive: the rule counts `{}` as unset), and zizmor `dangerous-triggers` when the output keeps `pull_request_target` and the answer states why (Collaborators-only PR access, or private repo with the split-job pattern).
The hand-back explains, in one line each, the reason for every opinionated default it applied.
The answer asks only about decisions the repo cannot answer (or states none were needed); it does not ask the user for facts it could look up.

The transcript shows every commit SHA written into a `uses:` line came from running `pinact run` on the file; no `gh api` call (`git/refs/tags`, `/commits/`, `/releases`) or other hand lookup produced a SHA that was then typed into the YAML.

evals.prompt: Add a workflow that builds my Docker image on PRs and publishes it to ghcr.io on main and semver tags. Use the repository name for the image. Save it as docker.yml.
evals.expected_output: A Docker workflow that builds without pushing on PRs, publishes to GHCR on trusted refs, uses Buildx, metadata-action, build-push-action, GHA cache, scoped package permissions, and provenance/SBOM.
expectations: The workflow builds on pull requests and pushes to main and semver-style tags.

Image push, provenance, and SBOM happen only on trusted refs (push to the default branch or a semver tag). The pull_request path builds with push: false in a job that holds no packages: write; the job that pushes is the only one granted packages: write and does not run on pull_request events. A single job with `push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` and packages: write on every event fails this.
The image publishing job grants packages: write without granting broad write-all permissions.
The workflow uses Buildx cache and enables provenance and SBOM for published images.

The workflow is saved as docker.yml and the image name derives from the repository (`${{ github.repository }}` or `ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}` in metadata-action `images:`), as the prompt asked.

evals.prompt: Audit this workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml, attached) for security problems. Give me a report of what is wrong and a corrected version.

expectations: The report identifies pull_request_target combined with checking out the PR head as a critical risk and moves the workflow to pull_request or isolates the untrusted checkout.

The report identifies the PR title interpolated directly into a run: block as template injection, and the corrected workflow no longer interpolates it into a shell (passed through env, or the step removed).
The corrected workflow replaces permissions: write-all with permissions: {} at the top and explicit per-job grants.
The corrected workflow pins actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to full commit SHAs with a version comment.
The report separates tool-backed or rule-backed hard findings from opinion or style items under distinct headings.

The report's Tools line names actionlint, shellcheck, zizmor, poutine, pinact, gasa, and run-stats, each as ran, 'absent', or 'skipped: <reason>'; a sentence that only says the scanners were run fails this.

The corrected workflow still does what the original did: tests run on the same events, and the PR comment step is kept in a safe shape (env-passed values, no pull_request_target) or its removal is stated with the reason. Correctness names the step that can never succeed as written: `gh pr comment` also runs on `push` events, where there is no PR number.

If pinact moved an action to a newer major than the original (`@v4` becomes a `# v7.x` comment), the hand-back names each such action and gives the command that keeps the old major (`scripts/scan.sh pinact run -update -min-age 7 -i 'actions/checkout@v4' <file>`); silent major jumps fail this.

The report flags the upload-artifact line whose version comment carries extra text after the version (Dependabot skips updating a comment with anything besides the version, so the pin silently goes stale), and in the corrected file that comment is the version alone.

evals.prompt: Our CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, attached) takes about 25 minutes on every push and people have started ignoring it. Speed it up without dropping real coverage.
evals.expected_output: A faster workflow that adds concurrency cancellation, npm caching, timeouts, drops the redundant fetch-depth: 0 and duplicate matrix cell, runs lint and test in parallel, adds Buildx cache for the image build, keeps the existing pins and permissions, and explains why each change helps.
expectations: The workflow gains a concurrency block with cancel-in-progress for superseded runs.
setup-node gains cache: npm or an equivalent package-manager cache.

Only the redundant matrix alias is removed: ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04 are the same runner today, so one of them goes; ubuntu-22.04 is a distinct runner and stays, or its removal is proposed as a coverage question with the reason.
fetch-depth: 0 is removed from jobs that do not need history, or its removal is proposed with the reason.
Lint and test no longer run strictly sequentially, or the answer justifies keeping needs: lint.
Jobs gain timeout-minutes.
The docker build step moves to docker/setup-buildx-action and docker/build-push-action with type=gha cache, or the answer recommends that change.

The existing SHA pins are preserved exactly (same SHAs and version comments, including setup-node `# v4.4.0`; a whole-file `pinact -update` would have bumped it) and the permissions block is not loosened.
Each speed change is explained with the reason it saves time.
